items.reason: Passage confirms establishment in 1660 and address 120 Tremont Street; another passage confirms Samuel Adams, John Hancock, and Paul Revere are buried there.
Passage states King's Chapel was founded in 1686, is adjacent to Boston's oldest English burying ground, and lists address as 58 Tremont St.
Passage confirms Boston Latin School founded in 1635, marked by a mosaic and statue of Benjamin Franklin, located at 45 School St.
Passage confirms building constructed in 1718, home to Ticknor and Fields publishers, located at 283 Washington St.
Passage describes the district as a collection of late 19th/early 20th century industrial loft buildings with exterior work visible from public ways, and lists the Neighborhood as South Boston.
Passage confirms Martin's Park is located at 64 Sleeper Street on the South Boston waterfront and honors Martin W. Richard, the youngest victim of the Boston Marathon bombings.
